title: Pure infinitely self-modifying code
abstract: Formalizes the corrected construction of pure infinitely self-modifying code from Gregory Morse's 2018 paper. An unbounded integer-address machine simulates finite Turing machines, preserves halting and divergence, writes code at every computational instruction, and admits a run changing unboundedly many fetched code fields from a literal identity-memory initializer whose memory is proved primitive recursive. Terminal interpreter journals occur on reached halted configurations of the numbered interpreter on the encoded finite input. The development includes a four-register MOV foundation, effective finite-machine interpretation, tape and head observations, and conditional bounded x86/x64 instruction, relocation and native-trace refinements. Finite hardware is not claimed to have unbounded memory.
